text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- New law will allow bulk water users to choose suppliers and purification services. (p1)
- Amsterdam options exchange threatens to halt trade today, if volume of trade gets out of hand. (p1)
- Wholesale group Sligro exceeds its own profit forecast with strong growth. (p3)
- Rapid jobless decline seen in the first quarter slows down in the second. (p5)
- Junior finance minister Wim Vermeend studies ways to limit tax advantages enjoyed by the tobacco industry. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Swine fever outbreak in new area in the province of Gelderland. (p1)
- Unions and meat processing factory Dumeco reach agreement on social plan. (p2)
- Health insurer Zilveren Kruis seals contract with Boots, the British chain of dispensing chemists. (p3)
- Natural gas monopoly Gasunie loses another client to a British rival. (p13)
DE TELEGRAAF
- The Holland Media Group posts huge loss of 47 million guilders in 1996. (p1)
- House prices rise 12 pct in first half of 1997 compared to same period of 1996. (p1)
- Export industry chiefs demand parliamentary debate about stopping subsidies on exports to developing countries. (p29) TROUW
- Philips Electronics and Dutch PTT KPN
knew about Teleworld/Holland Media Group affaire in June. (p7) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Protests at stevedorer ECT over Bell Lijn lead to chaos in Rotterdam port area. (p11)
